app.quit.what: Close the workbench, stopping firmware on the way out.

board.screenshot.what: write the board's display to a PNG and return its path

params.name: node
params.what: the node whose screen to capture

firmware.details.what: Report everything known about one build: where it is, what it is, and what has been decided about it.

params.name: version
params.what: the build's version or imported label

params.name: role
params.what: which role, when one label carries more than one

params.name: board
params.what: which board; absent means a build for this machine

firmware.rescan.what: ask the catalogue what is published again, which is how a build nobody has downloaded becomes offerable

firmware.update.what: Rename a build, move it to another board or role, or change how it is run.

params.name: version
params.what: the build to change, by its current version or label

params.name: role
params.what: its current role, when one label carries more than one

params.name: board
params.what: its current board

params.name: label
params.what: rename it to this; unchanged when absent

params.name: new_role
params.what: run it as this role instead; unchanged when absent

params.name: new_board
params.what: move it to this board instead; unchanged when absent

params.name: card_required
params.what: this firmware will not get far without storage in the board's slot, so every node running it is given a card whatever it would otherwise have had

params.name: coproc_at_reset
params.what: start this build's coprocessors enabled, which the part does not do - for a firmware that traps inside its own exception vector and cannot be seen past

params.name: notes
params.what: what the next person should know about this build

firmware.window.what: Open one build's own window: what it is, where it lives, and how it is run.

params.name: version
params.what: the build's version or imported label

params.name: role
params.what: which role, when one label carries more than one

params.name: board
params.what: which board; absent means a build for this machine

map.centre.what: Point the map at a node, or at a latitude and longitude.

params.name: node
params.what: centre on this node instead of giving coordinates

params.name: lat
params.what: degrees north

params.name: lon
params.what: degrees east

params.name: zoom
params.what: zoom level; unchanged when absent

map.fit.what: Zoom the map so every node is on it.

node.card.what: Report or change what is in one node's card slot: whether a card is fitted, which file it is, and whether to erase it.

params.name: node
params.what: which node

params.name: fitted
params.what: put a card in the slot or take it out; unchanged when absent

params.name: file
params.what: the file behind the card; empty string returns it to the node's own, named after the node and kept beside its flash

params.name: wipe
params.what: erase the card, which is what reformatting one is

node.output.what: read what a node's serial port, emulator or radio model has printed

params.name: node
params.what: the node to read

params.name: source
params.what: serial, emulator or radio; serial by default

params.name: lines
params.what: how many lines of the tail to answer with, up to 2000

node.output_window.what: Open one node's one log in a window of its own, so a board's screen and several of its logs can be watched at once.

params.name: node
params.what: which node

params.name: source
params.what: which log: serial, rom, emulator, radio; serial when absent

node.window.what: Open one node's own window, the thing people put on a second monitor.

params.name: node
params.what: which node

params.name: tab
params.what: which tab to open on; the window's default when absent

node.wipe.what: erase one node's stored state: its flash, its card and its files

params.name: node
params.what: the node to put back to factory

panels.list.what: Name every panel the interface has registered.

session.checkpoint.what: freeze the whole session to a named checkpoint

params.name: name
params.what: what to call this checkpoint

session.checkpoints.what: list the checkpoints that can be restored

session.journal.what: every command this workbench has been driven with, newest last, and when the process started - so a session picked up cold can be told how the world got here, and whether it has been restarted

session.restore.what: rebuild a checkpoint and replay to the moment it was taken

params.name: name
params.what: the checkpoint to restore, by name

params.name: path
params.what: a checkpoint file kept outside the checkpoints directory

ui.keep_above.what: Say whether a window popped out of the workbench stays above it, and report the setting either way.

params.name: on
params.what: set it; omit to read the current setting without changing it

workspace.set.what: Show one of the workbench's top-level views.

params.name: view
params.what: the view's name, as panels.list and the view bar spell it
